security_audit.summary: The skill performs intended network calls to BrowserAct and requires a BrowserAct API key. Most static findings are Markdown formatting false positives, but the instructions and script create a real secret-handling concern by allowing users to provide an API key directly.

remediation.issue: The skill tells users they may provide the BrowserAct API key directly.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in their local environment and avoid pasting API keys into chat or logs.

remediation.issue: The skill sends search parameters and authentication to a third-party BrowserAct endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Clearly disclose that keywords, locale settings, and task metadata are sent to BrowserAct before execution.

remediation.issue: The documented command runs a local Python script that performs external API calls.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review the command and confirm they want to run the BrowserAct workflow before execution.

content.value_statement: Manual image search is slow when teams need repeatable visual research data. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow and returns structured Google Images metadata for analysis.
actual_capabilities: Runs a Python script that starts a BrowserAct Google Images workflow.
Accepts search keywords, country, language, scroll count, and result limit parameters.
Polls BrowserAct task status and prints timestamped progress messages.
Returns image result metadata such as title, source, thumbnail, and click-through link.
Guides users to configure the BROWSERACT_API_KEY environment variable.
limitations: Requires a valid BrowserAct API key before it can run.
Depends on BrowserAct API availability and the configured workflow template.
May take several minutes because it polls an external browser automation task.
Does not verify image copyright, licensing, or usage rights.

use_cases.title: Collect visual market signals
use_cases.description: Gather image titles, sources, thumbnails, and links for products or topics across selected regions.

use_cases.title: Monitor competitor imagery
use_cases.description: Search competitor names or product terms and review the visual assets that appear in Google Images.

use_cases.title: Build image research datasets
use_cases.description: Create repeatable lists of Google Images metadata for enrichment, trend review, or source discovery.

prompt_templates.title: Search one topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Google Images metadata for "modern office chair" using the default country and language.

prompt_templates.title: Search a local market
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect Google Images results for "electric bicycle" in Germany with German language settings.

prompt_templates.title: Limit result volume
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Google Images for "minimalist desk lamp" in the United States, scroll 3 times, and return up to 25 items.

prompt_templates.title: Compare regional visuals
prompt_templates.prompt: Run separate Google Images searches for "skincare packaging" in Japan, France, and the United States, then summarize source and style differences.

output_examples.input: Search for "running shoes" in the United States.
output_examples.output: A structured list of image results with titles, source names, thumbnail links, result indexes, and click-through URLs.

output_examples.input: Find "coffee packaging" image results for Japan with Japanese language settings.
output: A final metadata list for matching Google Images results
A short note if the BrowserAct task fails or times out

output_examples.input: Collect 20 image results for "solar panels" in France.
output_examples.output: A concise set of up to 20 result records that can be reviewed for visual research and source discovery.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY as an environment variable instead of pasting secrets into chat.
Use specific search terms, country codes, and language codes to improve result relevance.
Review returned links and thumbnails before using images in public materials.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to collect copyrighted images without checking usage rights.
Do not paste BrowserAct API keys into prompts, logs, or shared transcripts.
Do not run broad repeated searches without considering API cost and service limits.

faq.question: What does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches Google Images through a BrowserAct workflow and returns structured metadata from the results.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The script requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY to authenticate with the BrowserAct API.

faq.question: Can it download full images?
faq.answer: No. The documented output is metadata such as titles, sources, thumbnails, and click-through URLs.

faq.question: Can I choose a country or language?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill accepts country and language parameters for localized Google Images sessions.

faq.question: How long does a search take?
faq.answer: It can take several minutes because the script starts and polls an external browser automation task.

faq.question: Is this safe for sensitive searches?
faq.answer: Search terms and parameters are sent to BrowserAct. Avoid sensitive queries unless your organization approves that data sharing.
